coverage: All eighteen scenes: principal cast, differentiated namesakes, household and military speakers, civic crowd, apparition and named references.

entities.name: Marcus Brutus
entities.body: The Roman senator, Portia’s husband and the play’s central figure.

entities.name: Julius Caesar
entities.body: The Roman leader whose growing power divides Rome, and Calphurnia’s husband.

entities.name: Caius Cassius
entities.body: The Roman senator who urges Brutus to resist Caesar’s power.

entities.name: Mark Antony
entities.body: Caesar’s close ally, the Roman commander also called Antonius.

entities.name: Octavius Caesar
entities.body: Caesar’s adopted son and heir, the young Roman also called Octavius.

entities.name: Portia
entities.body: Brutus’s wife and Cato’s daughter.

entities.name: Casca
entities.body: The Roman who reports Caesar’s reception by the crowd to Brutus and Cassius.

entities.name: Calphurnia
entities.body: Caesar’s wife.

entities.name: Decius Brutus
entities.body: The Roman associate of Cassius, distinct from Marcus Brutus.

entities.name: Metellus Cimber
entities.body: The Roman whose brother Publius Cimber is in exile.

entities.name: Trebonius
entities.body: One of the Romans in Cassius’s circle.

entities.name: Cicero
entities.body: The Roman senator and celebrated orator.

entities.name: Caius Ligarius
entities.body: The ailing Roman whom Brutus summons to his house.

entities.name: Artemidorus
entities.body: The man carrying a written warning for Caesar.

entities.name: Lepidus
entities.body: The Roman political leader associated with Antony and Octavius.

entities.name: Publius
entities.body: The elderly senator accompanying Caesar to the Capitol.

entities.name: Popilius Lena
entities.body: The senator who speaks to Cassius on the way to the Capitol.

entities.name: Marullus
entities.body: One of the tribunes challenging the celebrations in Caesar’s honor.

entities.name: Flavius, the tribune
entities.body: The tribune who confronts the workers celebrating Caesar.

entities.name: Lucius
entities.body: Brutus’s young servant, who also plays music for him.

entities.name: Lucilius
entities.body: An officer serving Brutus.

entities.name: Titinius
entities.body: The Roman associated with Cassius and Brutus, also named in Cassius’s recollection of Caesar.

entities.name: Messala
entities.body: The officer who brings military and political news to Brutus.

entities.name: Pindarus
entities.body: Cassius’s servant, whom Cassius took captive in Parthia.

entities.name: Young Cato
entities.body: The younger Marcus Cato, Portia’s brother, fighting with Brutus.

entities.name: Flavius, the officer
entities.body: An officer in Brutus’s army, distinct from the opening tribune.

entities.name: Labeo
entities.body: The officer whom Brutus orders to arrange his forces.

entities.name: Clitus
entities.body: One of Brutus’s attendants on the battlefield.

entities.name: Dardanius
entities.body: An attendant accompanying Brutus in the final scene.

entities.name: Strato
entities.body: One of Brutus’s attendants.

entities.name: Volumnius
entities.body: Brutus’s former schoolmate and battlefield companion.

entities.name: Varro
entities.body: One of Brutus’s servants, stationed in his tent.

entities.name: Claudius
entities.body: The servant who shares the watch in Brutus’s tent with Varro.

entities.name: Statilius
entities.body: The man sent ahead to signal to Brutus with a torch.

entities.name: Cinna
entities.body: The Roman meeting with Cassius and his associates.

entities.name: Cinna the poet
entities.body: The poet who shares a name with Cinna in Cassius’s circle.

entities.name: The Soothsayer
entities.body: The diviner warning Caesar about the Ides of March.

entities.name: The carpenter
entities.body: The worker whom the tribunes question in the opening street scene.

entities.name: The cobbler
entities.body: The shoemaker who answers the tribunes with puns.

entities.name: Caesar’s servant
entities.body: The household servant sent to consult the priests.

entities.name: Antony’s servant
entities.body: The messenger sent to speak for Antony before he approaches Brutus.

entities.name: Octavius’s servant
entities.body: The messenger reporting Octavius’s movements to Antony.

entities.name: The poet in the camp
entities.body: The poet who interrupts Brutus and Cassius in their tent.

entities.name: The battlefield messenger
entities.body: The messenger reporting the enemy’s advance to Antony and Octavius.

entities.name: The first camp soldier
entities.body: One of the soldiers calling the halt outside Brutus’s tent.

entities.name: The second camp soldier
entities.body: Another soldier passing the order to halt in the camp.

entities.name: The third camp soldier
entities.body: The third soldier repeating the command to halt.

entities.name: Antony’s first soldier
entities.body: The soldier confronting Lucilius on the battlefield.

entities.name: Antony’s second soldier
entities.body: The soldier calling for Antony during Lucilius’s capture.

entities.name: The first citizen
entities.body: One of the numbered voices of the Roman crowd in the Forum and street scenes.

entities.name: The second citizen
entities.body: One of the numbered voices of the Roman crowd in the Forum and street scenes.

entities.name: The third citizen
entities.body: One of the numbered voices of the Roman crowd in the Forum and street scenes.

entities.name: The fourth citizen
entities.body: One of the numbered voices of the Roman crowd in the Forum and street scenes.

entities.name: The Roman citizens
entities.body: The crowd of ordinary Romans addressed by the political leaders.

entities.name: Caesar’s ghost
entities.body: The apparition of Caesar that appears to Brutus.

entities.name: Pompey
entities.body: The Roman commander and political rival of Caesar recalled by the speakers.

entities.name: Lucius Junius Brutus
entities.body: The earlier Brutus associated with expelling Rome’s kings.

entities.name: Tarquin
entities.body: The last king of Rome, recalled in Brutus’s account of his ancestors.

entities.name: Marcus Cato
entities.body: Portia’s father and the father of young Cato, the Roman opponent of Caesar.

entities.name: Publius Cimber
entities.body: Metellus Cimber’s exiled brother.

entities.name: Publius, Antony’s nephew
entities.body: The son of Antony’s sister, named in the discussion of proscription.

entities.name: Lepidus’s brother
entities.body: The brother mentioned in the leaders’ discussion of proscription.

entities.name: Antony’s sister
entities.body: Publius’s mother, named through her relationship to Antony.

entities.name: Lucius Pella
entities.body: The Roman whom Brutus has condemned for taking bribes at Sardis.

entities.name: Epicurus
entities.body: The Greek philosopher whose teachings Cassius discusses.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.body: The Trojan hero who carries his father from burning Troy.

entities.name: Anchises
entities.body: Aeneas’s father, carried to safety in Cassius’s comparison.

entities.name: Ate
entities.body: The goddess of ruin invoked in Antony’s prediction of vengeance.

entities.name: Plutus
entities.body: The classical god of wealth, invoked by Cassius.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The divine powers associated with the course and end of human lives.

entities.name: The gods
entities.body: The divine powers invoked in the Romans’ prayers and oaths.

entities.name: The slave in Casca’s report
entities.body: The man whose burning but unharmed hand Casca describes as an omen.

entities.name: The women in Casca’s report
entities.body: The frightened women said by Casca to have seen men walking in flames.
